title: dialog Module
content_markdown:
The dialog module provides dialog awareness to the OpenSIPS proxy. Its functionality is to keep trace of the current dialogs, to offer information about them (like how many dialogs are active).

Aside tracking, the dialog module offers functionalities like flags and attributes per dialog (persistent data across dialog), dialog profiling and dialog termination (on timeout base or external triggered).

The module, via an internal API, also provide the foundation to build on top of it more complex dialog-based functionalities via other OpenSIPS modules.
overview:
The dialog module provides dialog awareness to the OpenSIPS proxy. Its functionality is to keep trace of the current dialogs, to offer information about them (like how many dialogs are active).

Aside tracking, the dialog module offers functionalities like flags and attributes per dialog (persistent data across dialog), dialog profiling and dialog termination (on timeout base or external triggered).

The module, via an internal API, also provide the foundation to build on top of it more complex dialog-based functionalities via other OpenSIPS modules.
how_it_works:
To create the dialog associated with an initial request, you must call the create_dialog() function, with or without parameter.

The dialog is automatically terminated when a “BYE” is received. In case of no “BYE”, the dialog lifetime is controlled via the default timeout (see “default_timeout” - default_timeout) and custom timeout (see “$DLG_timeout” - $DLG_timeout).

Once terminated, the in-memory dialog may be destroyed right away or, depending on the “delete_delay” - delete_delay) setting, it may be kept for a while in memory, in a read-only state (no action, no changes, nothing). This delaying may be used to help with the routing of late in-dialog request that may be received after the dialog terminted (like late BYE's due retransmissions, cross BYE requests, auth'ed BYE request, slow ACK on re-INVITEs, etc).

dependencies_required.name: RR
dependencies_required.reason: Record-Route module, optional, if Dialog ID matching is used in non Topo Hiding cases

dependencies_required.name: clusterer
dependencies_required.reason: if replication_cluster parameter is set (contact replication via clusterer module)

exported_parameters.name: enable_stats
exported_parameters.description: If the statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistic variables, the module provide information about the dialog processing. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the dialogs. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of 2 number.
exported_parameters.notes: IMPORTANT: If dialogs' information should be stored in a database, a constant hash\_size should be used, otherwise the restored process will not take place. If you really want to modify the hash\_size you must delete all table's rows before restarting OpenSIPS.

exported_parameters.name: log_profile_hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table internally used to store profile->dialog associations. A larger table can provide more parallel operations but consumes more memory. The hash size is provided as the base 2 logarithm(e.g. log\_profile\_hash\_size =4 means the table has 2^4 entries).

exported_parameters.name: rr_param
exported_parameters.description: Name of the Record-Route parameter to be added with the dialog cookie. It is used for fast dialog matching of the sequential requests.

exported_parameters.name: default_timeout
exported_parameters.description: The default dialog timeout (in seconds) if no custom one is set.

exported_parameters.name: dlg_extra_hdrs
exported_parameters.description: A string containing the extra headers (full format, with EOH) to be added in the requests generated by the module (like BYEs).

exported_parameters.name: dlg_match_mode
exported_parameters.description: How the seqential requests should be matched against the known dialogs. The modes are a combination between matching based on a cookie (DID) stored as cookie in Record-Route header and the matching based on SIP elements (as in RFC3261).
exported_parameters.notes: NOTE that if you have call looping on your OpenSIPS server (passing more than once through the same OpenSIPS instance), it is strongly suggested to use only DID\_ONLY mode, as the SIP based matching will have an undefined behavior - from SIP perspective, a sequential dialog will match all the loops of the call, as the Call-ID, To and From TAGs are the same.

exported_parameters.name: delete_delay
exported_parameters.description: The interval (seconds) to delay a dialog deletion / removal from memory AFTER its termination. Once terminated, the dialog will be kept in a read only state (no action, no changes), but it will still be able to match and route late in-dialog requests.
exported_parameters.notes: This global value may be per-call changed via the DLG\_del\_delay “$DLG\_del\_delay” ([$DLG\_del\_delay](#pv_DLG_del_delay "1.10.9.�$DLG_del_delay")) script variable.

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: If you want to store the information about the dialogs in a database a database url must be specified.

exported_parameters.name: db_mode
exported_parameters.description: Describe how to push into the DB the dialogs' information from memory.

exported_parameters.name: db_update_period
exported_parameters.description: The interval (seconds) at which to update dialogs' information if you chose to store the dialogs' info at a given interval. A too short interval will generate intensive database operations, a too large one will not notice short dialogs.

exported_parameters.name: options_ping_interval
exported_parameters.description: The interval (seconds) at which OpenSIPS will generate in-dialog OPTIONS pings for one or both of the involved parties.

exported_parameters.name: reinvite_ping_interval
exported_parameters.description: The interval (seconds) at which OpenSIPS will generate in-dialog Re-INVITE pings for one or both of the involved parties.
exported_parameters.notes: Important: the ping timeout detection is performed every time this interval ticks, not when the re-INVITE transaction times out! Consequently, please make sure that the timeouts for re-INVITE transactions (e.g. the "fr_timeout" modparam of the "tm" module or its $T_fr_timeout variable) are always lower than the value of this parameter! Failing to ensure this ordering of timeouts may possibly lead to re-INVITE pings never ending a disconnected dialog due to pings getting retried before getting a chance to properly time out.

exported_parameters.name: profiles_with_value
exported_parameters.description: List of names (alphanumerical) for profiles with values. Flags _/b_ or _/s_ allow sharing profiles between OpenSIPS instances using the clusterer module or a CacheDB backend, respectively.

exported_parameters.name: profiles_no_value
exported_parameters.description: List of names (alphanumerical) for profiles without values. Flags _/b_ or _/s_ allow sharing profiles between OpenSIPS instances using the clusterer module or a CacheDB backend, respectively.

exported_parameters.name: db_flush_vals_profiles
exported_parameters.description: Pushes dialog values, profiles and flags into the database along with other dialog state information (see db\_mode 1 and 2).

exported_parameters.name: timer_bulk_del_no
exported_parameters.description: The number of dialogs that should be attempted to be deleted at the same time ( a single query ) from the DB back-end.

exported_parameters.name: race_condition_timeout
exported_parameters.description: If dialog is created using the 'E' flag, and a SIP Race condition happens, then the dialog will be terminated after 'race_condition_timeout' seconds. Currently, the only supported race conditions are (200OK vs CANCEL) and (early BYE vs 200OK)

exported_parameters.name: cachedb_url
exported_parameters.description: Enables distributed dialog profiles and specifies the backend that should be used by the CacheDB interface.

exported_parameters.name: profile_value_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Specifies what prefix should be added to the profiles with value when they are inserted into CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

exported_parameters.name: profile_no_value_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Specifies what prefix should be added to the profiles without value when they are inserted into CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

exported_parameters.name: profile_size_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Specifies what prefix should be added to the entity that holds the profiles with value size in CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

exported_parameters.name: profile_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Specifies how long a dialog profile should be kept in the CacheDB until it expires. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

exported_parameters.name: dialog_replication_cluster
exported_parameters.description:
Specifies the cluster ID for dialog replication using the _clusterer_ module. This enables sending and receiving all the dialog-related events (creation, update and deletion) in the cluster.

This OpenSIPS cluster exposes the **"dialog-dlg-repl"** capability in order to mark nodes as eligible for becoming data donors during an arbitrary sync request. Consequently, the cluster must have _at least one node_ marked with the **"seed"** value as the _clusterer.flags_ column/property in order to be fully functional. Consult the [clusterer - Capabilities](clusterer#capabilities) chapter for more details.

exported_parameters.name: profile_replication_cluster
exported_parameters.description: Specifies the cluster ID for profile replication using the _clusterer_ module. This enables sending and receiving the profile information (value, dialog count) in the cluster.

exported_parameters.name: replicate_profiles_buffer
exported_parameters.description: Used to specify the length of the buffer used by the binary replication, in bytes. Usually this should be big enough to hold as much data as possible, but small enough to avoid UDP fragmentation. The recommended value is the smallest MTU between all the replication instances.

exported_parameters.name: replicate_profiles_check
exported_parameters.description: Timer in seconds, used to specify how often the module should check whether old, replicated profiles values are obsolete and should be removed. should replicate its profiles to the other instances.

exported_parameters.name: replicate_profiles_timer
exported_parameters.description: Timer in milliseconds, used to specify how often the module should replicate its profiles to the other instances.

exported_parameters.name: replicate_profiles_expire
exported_parameters.description: Timer in seconds, used to specify when the profiles counters received from a different instance should no longer be taken into account. This is used to prevent obsolete values, in case an instance stops replicating its counters.

exported_parameters.name: cluster_auto_sync
exported_parameters.description: Specifies whether to automatically issue a sync request (for dialogs marked with a sharing tag in backup state) when a node becomes reachable. A value of _1_ means enabled and _0_ disabled.

exported_functions.name: create_dialog

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Optionally,the function also receives a string parameter, which specifies special behavior to be done for the current dialog.

return_values.condition: if the dialog was successfully created or if the dialog was previously created

exported_functions.description: The function creats the dialog for the currently processed request. The request must be an initial request. Optionally,the function also receives a string parameter, which specifies special behavior to be done for the current dialog.

exported_functions.name: match_dialog

parameters.name: dlg_match_mode
parameters.description: A specific matching mode may be enforced by specifying the optional "dlg_match_mode" parameter.

return_values.condition: if a dialog exists for the request

exported_functions.description: This function is to be used to match a sequential (in-dialog) request to an ongoing dialog. By default, dialog matching is performed according to the dlg_match_mode module parameter. A specific matching mode may be enforced by specifying the optional "dlg_match_mode" parameter. Possible values for this parameter are "DID_ONLY", "DID_FALLBACK" and "DID_NONE". As sequential requests are automatically matched to the dialog when doing "loose_route()" from script, this function is intended to: (A) control the place in your script where the dialog matching is done and (B) to cope with bogus sequential requests that do not have Route headers, so they are not handled by loose_route().

exported_functions.name: validate_dialog

return_values.condition: if a dialog exists for the request and if the request is valid (according to dialog data)
other errors ( parsing, no dlg, etc )

exported_functions.description: The function checks the current received requests against the dialog (internal data) it belongs to. Performing several tests, the function will help to detect the bogus injected in-dialog requests (like malicious BYEs). The performed tests are related to CSEQ sequence checking and routing information checking (contact and route set).

exported_functions.name: fix_route_dialog
exported_functions.description: The function forces an in dialog SIP message to contain the ruri, route headers and dst_uri, as specified by the internal data of the dialog it belongs to. The function will prevent the existence of bogus injected in-dialog requests ( like malicious BYEs )

exported_functions.name: get_dialog_info

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: the name of the dialog variable (from the found dialog) to be returned

parameters.name: avp
parameters.description: an avp where to store the values of the "attr" dialog variable. Since the function checks through all dialogs, this needs to be an actual AVP in order to support pushing values from all matched dialogs.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: name of a dialog variable to be used a search key (when looking after the target dialog)

parameters.name: key_val
parameters.description: the value of the dialog variable that is used as key in searching the target dialog.

parameters.name: no_dlgs
parameters.description: the total number of dialogs containing the key variable

exported_functions.description: The function extracts a dialog value from another dialog. It first searches through all existing (ongoing) dialogs for all dialogs that have a dialog variable named "key" with the value "key_val" (so a dialog where $dlg_val(key)=="key_val"). If found, it returns the value of the dialog variable "attr" from all the founds dialog in the "avp" pseudo-variable, otherwise nothing is written in "avp", and a negative error code is returned. NOTE: the function does not require to be called in the context of a dialog - you can use it whenever / whereever for searching for other dialogs.

exported_functions.name: get_dialog_vals

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: an AVP variable to hold all the names of the variables from the found dialog.

parameters.name: vals
parameters.description: an AVP variable to hold all the values of the variables from the found dialog.

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: the callid of a dialog to be searched (and have the variables fetched).

exported_functions.description:
The function fetches all the dialog variables of another dialog. It first searches through all existing (ongoing) dialogs based on the given SIP CallID. If found, it returns all the dialog variables as two parallel arrays of names and values (using the given variables "names" and "vals"). As these variables have to hold arrays, they must be AVPs.

NOTE: the function does not require to be called in the context of a dialog - you can use it whenever / whereever for searching for other dialogs.

examples.description: Fetches and logs dialog variables for a specific Call-ID.

exported_functions.name: get_dialogs_by_val

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the dialog variable used for the lookup

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the value of the above dialog val

parameters.name: out_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will be populated will the dialog JSONs for all the matched calls

parameters.name: out_dlg_no
parameters.description: the out var which will contain the total number of matched dialogs

exported_functions.description:
The function looks up through the whole dialog table for dialogs containing a $dlg_val with the provided name and value, and returns all the $DLG_ctx_json variables for the matched dialogs, storing them in the provided out_avp. The total number of matched dialogs is returned in the out_dlgs_no variable

NOTE: the function does not require to be called in the context of a dialog - you can use it whenever / whereever for searching for other dialogs.

examples.description: Searches for dialogs by a specific variable value and processes the results.

exported_functions.name: get_dialogs_by_profile

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name of the dialog profile used for the lookup

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: the value of the above dialog profile ( optional )

parameters.name: out_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will be populated will the dialog JSONs for all the matched calls

parameters.name: out_dlg_no
parameters.description: the out var which will contain the total number of matched dialogs

exported_functions.description:
The function looks up through the whole dialog table for dialogs configured to be within the provided dialog profile name, and optionally with the provided profile value. The function returns all the $DLG_ctx_json variables for the matched dialogs, storing them in the provided out_avp. The total number of matched dialogs is returned in the out_dlgs_no variable

NOTE: the function does not require to be called in the context of a dialog - you can use it whenever / whereever for searching for other dialogs.

examples.description: Searches for dialogs by profile and value.

exported_functions.name: load_dialog_ctx

parameters.name: dialog
parameters.description: the identifier of the dialog to be loaded, it may be a SIP Call-ID or a Dialog ID.

parameters.name: id_type
parameters.description: what kind of dialog identified was used in the first parameter. It can be callid (SIP Call-ID) or did (internal Dialog ID). By default callid will be assumed.

exported_functions.description:
The function loads and switches to the context of the given dialog. The context of a dialog is given by the dialog flags, variables, profiles and any other value/state related to the dialog. By switching to the context of another dialog, you will see at the script level, by default, all the data from the new dialog.

NOTE: you cannot perform a new load until doing an unload - no nested loadings are possible.

examples.description: Loads a dialog context by Call-ID and logs its duration and profile status.

exported_functions.name: unload_dialog_ctx
exported_functions.description:
The function off-loads the loaded context of another dialog, exposing whatever dialog context was present before doing the load.

NOTE: you MUST perform from script an explicit unload for each load you did, otherwise the loaded dialog will remain hanged for ever.

examples.code: unload_dialog_ctx();
examples.description: Unloads the currently loaded dialog context.

exported_functions.name: set_dlg_profile

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: name of the profile to be added to.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: string value to define the belonging of the dialog to the profile - note that the profile must support values.

parameters.name: clear_values
parameters.description: if set to true (1), all values of the profile will be cleared before setting the given value.

exported_functions.description:
Inserts the current dialog into a profile. Note that if the profile does not support values, this will be silently discarded. A dialog may be inserted in the same profile multiple times.

NOTE: the dialog must be created before using this function (use create_dialog() function before).

exported_functions.name: unset_dlg_profile

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: name of the profile to be removed from.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description:
string value to define the belonging of the dialog to the profile - note that the profile must support values.

NEW in 3.4: for profiles with value, by omitting this parameter you can now clear all values of the given profile.

exported_functions.description:
Removes the current dialog from a profile.

NOTE: the dialog must be created before using this function (use create_dialog() function before).

exported_functions.name: is_in_profile

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: name of the profile to be checked against.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: string value to toughen the check.

exported_functions.description:
Checks if the current dialog belongs to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - if the dialog was inserted into the profile for a specific value. If no value is passed, only simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that if the profile does not support values, this will be silently discarded.

NOTE: the dialog must be created before using this function (use create_dialog() function before).

exported_functions.name: get_profile_size

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: name of the profile to get the size for.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: string value to toughen the check.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: an AVP or script variable to return the profile size in.

exported_functions.description: Returns the number of dialogs belonging to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - how many dialogs were inserted into the profile with a specific value. If not value is passed, only simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that the profile does not supports values, this will be silently discarded.

exported_functions.name: set_dlg_flag

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: The flag name.

exported_functions.description:
Sets the dialog flag named flag to true. The dialog flags are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (set and test) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

NOTE: the dialog must be created before using this function (use create_dialog() function before).

examples.code: set_dlg_flag("MY_DLG_FLAG");

exported_functions.name: set_dlg_sharing_tag

parameters.name: tag_name
parameters.description: The tag name.

exported_functions.description:
Marks the current dialog with the sharing tag _tag_name_. From this point on, actions like in-dialog pinging, BYEs on timeout etc. will depend on the tag state(no action in "backup" state, normal operation in "active" state).

For more details see the [Dialog clustering](#dialog-clustering "1.4.�Dialog clustering") chapter.

examples.code: set_dlg_sharing_tag("vip1");

exported_functions.name: dlg_on_answer

parameters.name: route_name
parameters.description: the name of the script route to be executed.

exported_functions.description:
The function arms a script route to be executed when the current dialog will be later answered. When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one).

You must use this function AFTER creating the dialog and before the dialog being answered.

If the parameter is missing, the function does a reset of any route previously set; there will be no triggering.

exported_functions.name: dlg_on_timeout

parameters.name: route_name
parameters.description: the name of the script route to be executed.

exported_functions.description:
The function arms a script route to be executed when (and if) the current dialog will timeout (as duration). When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one)

When the route is executed, the dialog is not yet terminated, just its lifetime reached the set limit. In the timeout route you can increase the dialog expiration timeout (and the dialog will continue) or you can let the dialog to be terminated (after the end of this route).

You must use this function AFTER creating the dialog and before the dialog being answered.

exported_functions.name: dlg_on_hangup

parameters.name: route_name
parameters.description: the name of the script route to be executed.

exported_functions.description:
The function arms a script route to be executed when the current dialog will be terminated. When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one). Note that the dialog will be already terminated and there is nothing you can do about it besides reading data from its context.

You must use this function AFTER creating the dialog and before the dialog being answered.

If the parameter is missing, the function does a reset of any route previously set; there will be no triggering.

exported_functions.name: dlg_send_sequential

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: the method of the request sent.

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg where the request is sent. Must be either _caller_ or _callee_.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: an optional body sent in the request. If missing, no body is sent.

parameters.name: content-type
parameters.description: the content type of the body sent. Make sure you specify this every time you send a request with a body, otherwise there are high changes that your UAC will reject the request.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: additional headers attached to the request sent.

exported_functions.description: Used to send an in-dialog request towards one if the dialog's legs. The function assumes that is runs inside a dialog context - if you are running it from a different context (such as an event_route), make sure you first load the dialog context using the [load_dialog_ctx()](#func_load_dialog_ctx "1.7.9.� load_dialog_ctx( dialog [, id_type])") function.

examples.description: Example 1.77. `dlg_send_sequential` usage to convert DTMF codes

exported_mi_functions.name: dlg_list

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: callid if a single dialog to be listed.

parameters.name: from_tag
parameters.description: fromtag (as per initial request) of the dialog to be listed.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: offset where the dialog listing should start.

parameters.name: counter
parameters.description: how many dialogs should be listed (starting from the offset)

exported_mi_functions.description: Lists the description of the dialogs (calls). If no parameter is given, all dialogs will be listed. If a dialog identifier is passed as parameter (callid and fromtag), only that dialog will be listed. If a index and conter parameter is passed, it will list only a number of "counter" dialogs starting with index (as offset) - this is used to get only section of dialogs.

examples.code: opensips-cli -x mi dlg_list
opensips-cli -x mi dlg_list callid=abcdrssfrs122444@192.168.1.1 from_tag=AAdfeEFF33
examples.description: list the dialog by callid and From TAG

examples.code: opensips-cli -x mi dlg_list index=40 counter=10
examples.description: list 10 dialogs, starting from the position 40 (in the list of all ongoing dialogs)

exported_mi_functions.name: dlg_list_ctx

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: callid if a single dialog to be listed.

parameters.name: from_tag
parameters.description: fromtag (as per initial request) of the dialog to be listed.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: offset where the dialog listing should start.

parameters.name: counter
parameters.description: how many dialogs should be listed (starting from the offset)

exported_mi_functions.description: The same as the “dlg_list” but including in the dialog description the associated context from modules sitting on top of the dialog module. This function also prints the dialog's values. In case of binary values, the non-printable chars are represented in hex (e.g. \x00)

examples.code: opensips-cli -x mi dlg_list_ctx

exported_mi_functions.name: dlg_end_dlg

parameters.name: dialog_id
parameters.description: this is an identifier of the dialog - it can be either (1) the unique ID of the dialog (as provided by dlg_list), either (2) the SIP Call-ID of the dialog.

parameters.name: extra_hdrs
parameters.description: string containg the extra headers (full format) to be added to the BYE requests.

exported_mi_functions.description: Terminates an ongoing dialog. If dialog is established, BYEs are sent in both directions. exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_count
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the number of current active dialogs (may be confirmed or not).

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_status
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the status of the dialog corresponding to the processed sequential request. This PV will be available only for sequential requests, after doing loose_route().

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_lifetime
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the duration (in seconds) of the dialog corresponding to the processed sequential request. The duration is calculated from the dialog confirmation and the current moment. This PV will be available only for sequential requests, after doing loose_route(). NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_flags
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the dialog flags (as a list of flag names separted by space) of the dialog corresponding to the processed sequential request. This PV will be available only for sequential requests, after doing loose_route(). NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_dir
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the direction of the request in dialog (as "upstream" string if the request is generated by callee or "downstream" string if the request is generated by caller) - to be used for sequential request. This PV will be available only for sequential requests (not for replies), after doing loose_route(). NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_did
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the id of the dialog corresponding to the processed sequential request. The output format is a string identical to the one returned by the dlg_list MI function. This PV will be available only for sequential requests, after doing loose_route(). NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_end_reason
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the reason for the dialog termination. It can be one of the following : * _Upstream BYE_ - Callee has sent a BYE * _Downstream BYE_ - Caller has sent a BYE * _Lifetime Timeout_ - Dialog lifetime expired * _MI Termination_ - Dialog ended via the MI interface * _Ping Timeout_ - Dialog ended because no reply to option pings * _ReINVITE Ping Timeout_ - Dialog ended because no reply to reinvite pings * _RTPProxy Timeout_ - Media timeout signaled by RTPProxy * _SIP Race Condition_ - SIP Race Condition occurred NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request, or if the dialog is not ended in the current context.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_timeout
exported_pseudo_variables.scope: initial requests (after dialog creation) or sequential requests (after loose_route)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Used to set the dialog lifetime (in seconds). When read, the variable returns the number of seconds until the dialog expires and is destroyed. Note that reading the variable is only possible after the dialog is created (for initial requests) or after doing loose_route() (for sequential requests). Important notice: using this variable with a REALTIME db_mode is very inefficient, because every time the dialog value is changed, a database update is done. NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request, otherwise the number of seconds until the dialog expiration.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_del_delay
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Used to set the dialog deletion delay (in seconds) for the current dialog (in a per-call manner). When read, the variable returns the number of seconds that were set for the call or the default value ( see the “delete_delay” - [delete_delay](#param_delete_delay "1.6.8.�delete_delay (integer)")) module param) for the delete delaying. The variable must be used when the context of a dialog is available in script.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_json
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The variable is read-only and exposes a JSON variable containing all the information that the dlg_list MI function contains NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request, otherwise the JSON will be returned.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $DLG_ctx_json
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The variable is read-only and exposes a JSON variable containing all the information that the dlg_list_ctx MI function contains ( on top of $DLG_json, this will expose the full list of dialog vars and profile links for the current dialog ) NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request, otherwise the JSON will be returned.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $dlg_val(name)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: This is a read/write variable that allows access to the dialog attribute named name. It can hold a string or integer value. This PV will be available only for sequential requests, after doing loose_route(). NULL will be returned if there is no dialog for the request.
